text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel resumed the transport of lorries on Thursday following a break of several hours caused by a power failure, a Eurotunnel spokeswoman said.
The lorry service was restored only last month on a trial basis following a blaze in the tunnel last November which caused 200 million pounds ($325 million) of damage and injured several people.
It was suspended again as a precaution on Thursday after a train carrying cars and passengers was trapped in the tunnel for 30 minutes on Thursday morning in an initial power failure.
witnesses on the train spoke of a flash and a loud bang but the Eurotunnel spokeswoman said there was no danger to passengers at any time.
Eurotunnel has been carrying lorries free of charge pending authorisation for a full resumption of freight traffic, which it hopes to receive by mid-June.
The freight business is seen as essential for Eurotunnel, struggling to secure shareholder and bank support for a plan to restructure its $12 billion debt.
Only two trains per hour ran each way through the tunnel while engineers worked on the power problem.

Car passengers with prior bookings were being taken through the tunnel but those without reservations were being redirected towards the ferries. This was expected to continue on Thursday evening while the backlog of lorries was cleared.
Eurotunnel is awaiting a report from a French investigating magistrate into the causes of the November 18 fire.
Authorisation for the full resumption of freight traffic depends on the outcome of a number of safety tests to be completed by June 15. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
